newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says Germany can still meet EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says Germany can still meet EMU goal.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Friday that he believed Germany could still meet Maastricht Treaty entry criteria for Europe's planned monetary union entry, albeit with some difficulty.
"It will be difficult for Germany to meet EMU deficits but it is still possible," Issing told journalists at a seminar on international monetary policy near Frankfurt.
He said a recent conclusion by six of Germany's top economic institutes that Germany would not meet the criteria were "premature".

The economic institutes had said on Tuesday that Germany's budget deficit was likely to be 3.5 percent of economic output in 1997, thus missing the 3.0 percent target set out in the Maastricht Treaty.

Asked by reporters to comment on the European Commission's decision this week to allow France to include a transfer of funds from France Telecom into efforts to reduce public deficits, Issing commented:
"This kind of precedent leads to a lack of clarity. The main factor in public finances is sustainability."
